name: Pipeline Without Automatic Hook Contract
storyIdentity: ENTITLED DRIVER ABANDONS CAR IN TRAFFIC (Ablation: Unconstrained Openers)
ablationHypothesis: The fatal narrative defects in Experiment B (the early arrest spoiler in Part 2 and the disjointed reverse-chronology in Part 1) were caused by the pipeline's automatic Hook Contract injecting hardcoded 'Barricaded door' anchor ranges (62-82s, 278-294s, 322-340s). Removing this single automatic constraint while keeping the rest of the pipeline identical will allow Gemini to discover natural chronological openers and protect Part 3's spoiler boundary.

promptDelta.removedBlock: Lines 14-40 of 01-gemini-highlight-scripts-prompt.txt (SERIES HOOK CONTRACT with userLocked=true anchors for candidate_004 [62-82s], candidate_015 [278-294s], candidate_017 [322-340s]).
promptDelta.addedBlock: Unconstrained series opener guidance: 'Each Part must discover its own strongest opening moment strictly inside its chronological scope. Strict Spoiler Ban: PART 1 and PART 2 must not depict or narrate the arrest, handcuffs, or charges.'
promptDelta.unalteredRules: One-scene-per-segment timestamp gate, 3-part serialization requirement, scene manifest mapping, action candidate coverage, voiceover length limits, output JSON schema.

parts.title: PART 1: ABANDONED ON THE HIGHWAY
parts.centralConflict: Deputy pulls up to clear traffic hazard; driver refuses help, leaves car in active lane and walks away.
parts.viewerQuestion: Why did she abandon her car in the middle of live highway lanes?

hook.quotedDialogue: This your car? What are you doing? / My car broke down. / I'm trying to help you get it out of the road. / You can't do anything... excuse me.

beats.voiceoverText: She storms away on foot, leaving her car blocking live traffic. But as deputies push it off the highway, she dials nine-one-one.
Instead of asking for roadside safety, she berates the dispatcher. Now, deputies are hunting down the runaway caller.

parts.climax: 911 recording where she threatens to hang up until she gets someone with a brain cell.
parts.payoff: Cliffhanger: Dispatch notifies deputies on scene that the 911 hangup is the same runaway driver.

parts.title: PART 2: THE SIDEWALK STANDOFF
parts.centralConflict: Deputies track down the runaway driver; she attempts to dismiss them and claims she's calling an Uber.
parts.viewerQuestion: Will deputies let her leave in an Uber?

hook.quotedDialogue: Alright ma'am stop, you are not free to go! You're not free to leave, do you understand? / Okay.

beats.voiceoverText: Cornered on a quiet residential sidewalk, she demands an Uber, completely unaware that emergency dispatchers have reported her calls.
Deputies have heard enough excuses. Her refusal to cooperate is about to trigger immediate legal consequences.

parts.climax: Deputy gives her a final warning that she cannot leave the scene.
parts.payoff: Cliffhanger right before the arrest: 'We're done talking now.'

parts.title: PART 3: THE 911 ARREST & PADDY WAGON
parts.centralConflict: Arrest execution and transport van confrontation over 911 emergency misuse.
parts.viewerQuestion: Does being rude to 911 constitute a criminal offense?

hook.quotedDialogue: So what am I being arrested for? / Misuse of 911.

beats.voiceoverText: She was booked for misdemeanor misuse of nine-one-one with bond set at five thousand dollars.

parts.climax: Transport van confrontation: 'My car was being towed by 911!' / '911 is for emergencies!'

editorialAssessment: Experiment C conclusively proves that removing the automatic Hook Contract eliminates the disastrous Part 2 spoiler and the backwards jump in Part 1. However, forcing the story into a 3-part series still creates unnecessary dilution across parts. Part 2 feels light on substance because the real meat of the story is only the highway walkaway (Part 1) and the arrest/van debate (Part 3).
